item.title: Scientists discover why some people still can’t taste food after COVID-19
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a possible explanation for why some people struggle to taste food more than a year after recovering from COVID-19. By examining taste buds from patients with lingering symptoms, researchers discovered molecular abnormalities that weaken the signals responsible for detecting sweet, bitter, and savory flavors. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Genomic study uncovers a new lace bug species on Japan's remote Ogasawara Islands
item.description: Researchers have used genome-wide DNA data to identify a new insect species on the Ogasawara Islands, a remote Japanese archipelago roughly 900 to 1,000 kilometers (560 to 620 miles) south of Tokyo. item.title: The race to power AI data centers is reshaping America's electric grid
item.description: AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting pressure on America’s power grid to modernize its equipment. Google says its planned 780MW data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google says it will support 1,900 megawatts of renewable energy and ways to protect local ratepayers. CNBC examines if projects like this can help upgrade the grid without shifting costs to residents. Fuente: CNBC - World.
